title: The Efficacy and Safety of Dalfampridine on Cognition and Fatigue in People With Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Halabi MH, Alromayan R, Almutairi M, Alasmari H, AlGhamdi MA, Makkawi S
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disease affecting the central nervous system. People with MS frequently experience cognitive dysfunction and fatigue. Dalfampridine (DAL), a potassium channel blocker, is US Food and Drug Administration-approved for the treatment of walking impairment in people with MS. It may also enhance nerve conduction in regions associated with fatigue and cognitive dysfunction. This study aims to evaluate DAL's efficacy in improving these symptoms, as well as its safety profile, in people with MS. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science, covering all records from database inception through April 1, 2024. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing DAL with placebo in people with MS and reporting impaired cognition and fatigue were included. A random-effects model was used to calculate the risk ratio (RR), standardized mean difference (SMD), and mean difference (MD) with 95% CIs. RESULTS: Of 1329 studies identified, 13 RCTs involving a total of 827 people with MS were included. DAL demonstrated a significant improvement in cognitive symptoms (SMD = 0.21; 95% CI, 0.04-0.38; P = .01; I² = 6%). However, no significant difference was observed between DAL and placebo in reducing fatigue (MD = 3.70; 95% CI, -4.37 to 11.77;P = .37; I² = 19%). Safety measures were comparable, with no significant difference in adverse events (RR = 1.11; 95% CI, 0.99-1.25; P = .08; I² = 0%). CONCLUSIONS: People with MS receiving DAL demonstrated significant improvement in cognitive symptoms; however, further studies are warranted to validate and confirm this finding.

title: Comorbid asthma - occurrence and associations with patient-related outcomes in COPD: a cohort study.
authors: Athlin Å, Lisspers K, Hasselgren M, Ställberg B, Sandelowsky H, Giezeman M, Janson C, Kisiel MA
journal: Scandinavian journal of primary health care
abstract: PURPOSE: Clinical features of COPD and asthma overlap, complicating differential diagnosis. This study investigated the prevalence of comorbid asthma in COPD patients and its association with patient-related outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients with a doctor's diagnosis of COPD were randomly selected in two cohorts 2005 (n = 1060) and 2014 (n = 1671), from primary and secondary care in Sweden. Data were collected from medical records and patient questionnaires at baseline and at follow-up (2012 and 2022, respectively). Questionnaires included data on exacerbations. Symptoms were assessed using the clinical COPD questionnaire (CCQ). Comorbid asthma was identified through medical records. Ten-year mortality data were obtained from national registers. Logistic and linear regression assessed associations with patient-reported outcomes; Cox regression was applied for mortality analyses. RESULTS: Comorbid asthma was found in 22% of the 2005 cohort and 9% of the 2014 cohort (p < .001). In both cohorts, it was associated with an increased risk of exacerbations: OR (95% CI) 1.58 (1.07-2.32), p = .02, and 2.20 (1.38-3.52), p < .001, respectively. No associations were found between comorbid asthma and worsening of health status (CCQ). Mortality risk did not differ in the 2005 cohort, HR (95% CI) 0.92 (0.71-1.18), but was lower in the 2014 cohort, HR (95% CI) 0.67 (0.49-0.93), p = .02. CONCLUSION: Comorbid asthma in COPD has changed from 22 to 9%, potentially due to improved diagnostics. Comorbid asthma remains clinically relevant due to its association with an increased exacerbation risk.

title: Differential mortality risks associated with ambient temperature among migrants and non-migrants: a space-time-stratified case-crossover study of the 100 Million Brazilian Cohort (2000-2020).
authors: Firouraghi N, Cortes TR, Jacobson LV, Neves DJD, Silveira IH, Hajat S, Barreto ML, Pescarini JM
abstract: BACKGROUND: Climate change disproportionately affects socially minoritized populations, but migrants' vulnerability to extreme temperatures remains overlooked. We estimated short-term associations between extreme ambient temperatures and mortality among migrants and non-migrants across Brazil. METHODS: We linked the 100 Million Brazilian Cohort to mortality and temperature data (2000-2020) and conducted a space-time-stratified case-crossover study analysing the differential effects of extreme temperature on mortality among internal migrants (i.e., Individuals whose state of birth was different from their residence at registration or death) and non-migrants. We used conditional quasi-Poisson regression with distributed lag non-linear model (DLNM) to estimate relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for all-cause non-accidental and cause-specific mortality associated with extreme-cold (1st percentile) and extreme-heat (99th percentile) compared to minimum-mortality-temperature (i.e., the temperature associated with the lowest mortality risk), over 0-20 days in both groups. We further stratified by age, literacy, urbanicity and housing conditions. FINDINGS: We included 1,199,636 deaths among internal-migrants (mean age at death = 62.67 years (standard-deviation (SD) = 18.36), with 673,166 (56%) males) and 3,716,900 deaths among non-migrants (57.18 years (SD = 20.31), with 2,135,293 (57%) males). Over 0-20 days, we observed a consistent pattern of higher risks of all-cause, non-accidental mortality among internal-migrants than non-migrants following both extreme-heat (RRMig(95%CI):1.05(1.01-1.10) vs. RRNon-mig:1.01(0.99-1.04)) and extreme-cold (RRMig:1.27(1.22-1.32) vs. RRNon-mig:1.24(1.20-1.28)). Extreme cold-related circulatory mortality (mortality due to diseases of the circulatory system, based on the relevant International Classification of Diseases codes) (I00-I99) was higher among non-migrants (RRMig:1.32(1.20-1.45) vs. RRNon-mig:1.41(1.31-1.51)) while heat-related respiratory mortality (J00-J99) was higher among internal-migrants (RRMig:1.32(1.10-1.58) vs. RRNon-mig:1.06(1.00-1.17)), particularly those illiterate (RRMig:1.84(1.25-2.71) vs. RRNon-mig:1.10(0.89-1.36)). Other subcategories showed greater 95%CI overlap. INTERPRETATION: We found internal migrants are likely to experience higher heat-related respiratory mortality than non-migrants particularly low-educated migrants. Our results highlight the need to further consider migrants for targeted climate adaptation policies, with a focus on reducing social inequalities in the place of arrival. FUNDING: The Wellcome Trust.

title: Evaluating a Modified American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status-Based Sedation Management System for Pancreatobiliary Endoscopy: A Prospective Feasibility Study.
authors: Hanaoka T, Okuwaki K, Watanabe M, Matsuda H, Adachi K, Tamaki A, Ogawa D, Sakai M
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To prospectively evaluate the feasibility of implementing a modified American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status (ASA-PS)-based sedation management system for endoscopist-managed sedation in pancreatobiliary endoscopy. METHODS: This single-center, single-arm prospective feasibility study involved 2000 patients (2024-2025). Sedation risk was stratified using a modified ASA-PS classification system combined with predefined high-risk clinical factors (severe obesity, obstructive sleep apnea requiring continuous positive airway pressure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease requiring home oxygen therapy, reduced functional capacity, and difficult sedation history). Patients meeting high-risk criteria underwent pre-procedural anesthesiologist assessment to determine sedation providers. The primary outcome was sedation-related adverse event (SRAE) incidence during endoscopist-managed sedation. The secondary outcomes were the sedation success rate and SRAE-associated risk factors. RESULTS: Among 2000 patients, 231 (11.6%) were classified as having high risk for sedation. Post-assessment, anesthesiologists and endoscopists managed sedation for 86 (4.3%) and 1914 (95.7%) patients, respectively. In the endoscopist-managed group, SRAEs occurred in 63 patients (3.3%), corresponding to a success rate of 96.7%. No patient required tracheal intubation or conversion to general anesthesia. In multivariable analysis, endoscopic ultrasonography-guided sampling was independently associated with reduced SRAEs (odds ratio 0.407, 95% confidence interval 0.184-0.899; p = 0.026); no independent predictors of increased SRAEs were identified. CONCLUSIONS: The modified ASA-PS-based sedation management system may be a feasible approach in settings with limited anesthesiology resources, warranting further validation. TRIAL REGISTRATION: UMIN000053211.

title: A topologically engineered hydrogel platform targeting IL11 promotes renal repair after partial nephrectomy.
authors: Yu Z, Dong X, Li F, Zhang Y, Dai S, Cao N, Jia X, Zhao J
abstract: Partial nephrectomy (PN) is the gold standard for treating renal tumors and trauma; however, massive nephron loss and persistent fibrosis readily lead to chronic kidney disease (CKD). Current therapeutic options remain non-curative and costly, as nearly half of PN patients inevitably progress to end-stage renal failure. Here, we present an innovative regenerative platform for PN-induced CKD, integrating structural biomimicry with targeted molecular inhibition. Harnessing light-based bioprinting of gelatin and hyaluronic acid methacrylates coupled with removable alginate microfiber, we constructed a hierarchical channel scaffold (HCS) that features precisely patterned macrochannels and template-derived microchannels, which closely mimics native kidney architecture, provides structural support, and remarkably enhances cell migration (∼5.45-fold) and rapid neovascularization (∼7.66-fold) over unidirectional channel structures. Moreover, interleukin 11 (IL11) was identified as a novel therapeutic target in kidney fibrosis after PN. Thus, extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem cells loaded with IL11 small interfering RNA (siIL11) were homogeneously encapsulated into HCS, achieving over 4-fold higher renal retention than systemic delivery in PN-induced CKD mice. Furthermore, sustained local release of EV-siIL11 and hierarchically channeled HCS guided synergistic regenerative effects that remarkably inhibited fibrosis, cell cycle arrest, and immune responses, thereby potently preventing kidney atrophy and restoring renal structure with newly aligned nephrons and vasculature, ultimately recovering kidney function. Further analysis revealed that IL11 silencing reversed epithelial‒mesenchymal transition by suppressing the STAT3-ERK-GSK3β-SNAI1 axis. This topological multifunctional hydrogel platform offers a localized, sustained, and clinically translatable strategy for postsurgical kidney regeneration.

title: Unsolved problems with ENaC: From molecules to mammals.
authors: Palmer LG
abstract: The epithelial Na channel (ENaC) mediates transport of Na+ in the kidney, the colon, the lung, and the sweat and salivary ducts. The activity of these channels is highly regulated and contributes to the maintenance of total body Na+, extracellular fluid volume, and plasma K+. Defects in the channel itself or in its regulation are implicated in hypertension and in other diseases. Despite progress in revealing many aspects of ENaC biology, many important questions remain unanswered. These include the following: What determines the remarkable ion selectivity of the channel? How is the channel directed to the apical plasma membrane? How does aldosterone regulate the channel? What is its role in producing urine with minimal Na+? And to what extent does the channel contribute to essential hypertension, cystic fibrosis, nephrotic syndrome, and liver failure? Here, I will discuss these questions and how they relate to our current understanding of the roles of ENaC in health and disease.

title: Spatial mechanopriming of multicellular interfaces drives cytoskeletal-to-nuclear remodeling to boost therapeutic efficacy of stem cells.
authors: Bayaraa O, Lee NH, Kim SH, Lee H, Li CJ, Fu X, Hyun J, Choi G
abstract: Engineering multicellular constructs through biophysical cues, independent of soluble biochemical factors, is a promising strategy to boost the therapeutic potential of stem cells for regenerative medicine. However, the mechanisms by which spatially organized cell-cell and cell-matrix interfaces govern multicellular signaling and subsequent behavioral outcomes remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate these mechanistic events by introducing 2D nanoplates (∼350 nm) compartmentalized within the intercellular space of mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) spheroids to form de novo cell-matrix spatial interfaces. These interfaces redistribute internal stress across the spheroid, amplifying integrin-cytoskeleton-nucleus force transmission and restoring YAP-dependent mechanotransduction to achieve spatial mechanopriming. Cells within these mechanoprimed spheroids exhibit profound nuclear deformation, epigenetic remodeling, and spatially patterned metabolic activation. Finite element modeling and spatial transcriptomic analyses further reveal a spheroid-wide reorganization of cytoskeletal and transcriptional networks. Mechanistically, elevated cytoskeletal tension across the reorganized interfaces is associated with a putative, tension-associated pseudo-hypoxic signature involving HIF-1α-related signaling, establishing a mechanometabolic niche that robustly enhances angiogenic secretion. Consequently, mechanoprimed spheroids demonstrate superior engraftment, accelerated vascular regeneration, and improved perfusion recovery in a murine ischemia model. Collectively, this work establishes spatial mechanopriming as an effective strategy to remodel cytoskeletal-to-nuclear mechanics and enhance the therapeutic potential of 3D multicellular systems.

title: Online chiral derivatization coupled with CE-MS for baseline separation of 16 proteinogenic amino acid enantiomers.
authors: Lu J, Gao W, Huang Q, Du L, Li H, Hu X, Wang C, Zhao Y
abstract: Amino acid (AA) enantiomers influence protein function through their distinct spatial structures, making their precise separation essential for elucidating physiological and pathological pathways. In this work, a novel method for the efficient separation of AA enantiomers based on on-line chiral derivatization with (S)-N-(4-nitrophenoxycarbonyl) phenylalanine methoxyethyl ester ((S)-NIFE) coupled with CE-MS has been developed. The method utilizes the ultrafast reaction kinetics of (S)-NIFE with AA enantiomers to facilitate their efficient separation. The online strategy eliminates time-consuming offline derivatization by permitting immediate injection upon simple mixing of derivatization reagent with AA enantiomers, enabling a streamlined analytical workflow. By optimizing experimental parameters, baseline separation of 16 chiral proteinogenic AA enantiomers has been achieved with resolutions ranging from 1.5 to 11.03. The relative standard deviations of migration time and peak area for intraday and interday measurements are less than 5%, and the limits of detection (LOD) and quantification (LOQ) are as low as 40 nM and 80 nM, respectively. Furthermore, the method was further applied to comparative analyses of AA enantiomers in serum samples from healthy controls and patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and atrial fibrillation. The baseline separation of three AA enantiomers was consistently achieved. The LODs and LOQs for three ᴅ-AAs in complex matrix were as low as 180 nM and 600 nM. The intraday and interday precisions were both below 11%, and the average recoveries range from 87.60% to 95.51% with low standard deviations. All these results confirm the effectiveness of the approach in separating AA enantiomers in complex matrices.

title: From laboratory quantification to rapid on-site testing: Screening of high-affinity monoclonal antibody pairs targeting the RSV F protein and analytical evaluation across multiple assay platforms.
authors: Peng S, Liu Q, Duan C, Liu J, Wang R, Huang Y, Long A, Deng Q
abstract: Monoclonal antibodies against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) F protein are key reagents for antigen-based diagnosis, yet antibody pairs compatible with multiple assay formats remain limited. In this study, BALB/c mice were immunized with recombinant postfusion RSV F protein, yielding six hybridoma cell lines secreting anti-RSV F monoclonal antibodies. The antibodies were characterized by indirect ELISA, Western blotting, and surface plasmon resonance, and the optimal sandwich pair was selected by cross-pairing ELISA. The mAb-14/mAb-26 pair showed high affinity and the best pairing performance and was used to establish double-antibody sandwich ELISA (DAS-ELISA), magnetic microparticle-based chemiluminescent immunoassay, and Au@Pt nanoparticle-based lateral flow immunoassay (Au@Pt-LFIA). The limits of detection were 0.25, 0.04, and 0.78 ng/mL, respectively. Au@Pt-LFIA achieved an approximately fourfold lower visual detection limit than conventional colloidal gold immunochromatography without additional signal-amplification steps. None of the three methods showed detectable cross-reactivity with the seven tested heterologous respiratory pathogen antigens. In preliminary clinical sample testing, the positive percent agreements of DAS-ELISA, chemiluminescent immunoassay, and Au@Pt-LFIA were 90.0%, 93.3%, and 83.3%, respectively, and the negative percent agreements were 100.0% for all methods. These results support mAb-14/mAb-26 as a versatile antibody pair for RSV antigen detection across complementary laboratory and on-site assay platforms.

title: Guanidine-quaternary ammonium polymer-derived carbon dots differentially modulate bacterial respiration and osteoblast mitochondria to resolve infection and foster osteointegration.
authors: Bai X, Qin A, Wang Z, Kong G, Zhang M, Li H, Zhao R, Yu Y
abstract: Implant-associated infections (IAIs) represent one of the most challenging complications following orthopedic implantation. Current antibacterial strategies struggle to achieve complete pathogen eradication while maintaining sustained osteogenic activity at the implant-bone interface. Leveraging the spatial divergence in energy metabolism between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, we designed and synthesized guanidine-quaternary ammonium polymer-derived carbon dots (GQCDs) with confirmed structure. Under non-infected conditions, GQCDs enhance mitochondrial metabolism to promote bone regeneration. In infected microenvironments, GQCDs not only selectively target bacterial membranes and inhibit the respiratory chain to exert potent antibacterial effects, but also downregulate host inflammatory responses and restore mitochondrial function in osteoblasts, thereby creating a favorable microenvironment for bone repair. GQCDs can be stably integrated onto various clinical implant substrates via a coating process. GQCDs-coated implants possessed the dual antibacterial and osteogenic functionalities, which were validated using in vitro co-culture systems and in vivo implant infection models in rats and beagles, offering a promising strategy with encouraging translational prospects to address IAIs.

title: Preliminary experience with controlled hypothermic storage of donor heart in combined heart transplantation.
authors: Argaw ST, Lora Ronco L, Frering A, Kloeckner M, Coutance G, Coilly A, Vibert E, Snanoudj R
abstract: While studies have demonstrated improved clinical outcomes with the use of controlled hypothermic storage (CHS) devices in isolated heart transplantation, it has not been evaluated in combined heart transplantation. In this small retrospective study (n=17), we evaluate clinical outcomes after combined heart-liver and heart-kidney transplantation in recipients of donor hearts preserved with conventional ice cold storage (ICS, n=10) versus CHS (n=7). The study found severe early graft dysfunction (EGD) occurred more frequently in the ICS cohort when compared to the CHS cohort (70% vs 0%, respectively). In addition, the CHS cohort had shorter median intensive care unit length of stay (7 days compared to 15.5 days, respectively) as well as fewer post-transplant complications, including sepsis (60% in ICS and 28.6% in CHS), pneumonia (40% in ICS and 14.3% in CHS), stroke (30% in ICS and 0% in CHS), and acute kidney injury requiring dialysis (60% in ICS and 28.6% in CHS). These preliminary findings suggest CHS may improve outcomes in combined heart transplantation.

title: Bioactive shape-memory biodegradable biliary stent functionalized with dHAM-Curcumin for improved biliary repair and microenvironment modulation.
authors: Dai C, Zhang H, Bai Y, Guan X, Li R, Quan D, Ding Y, Rao Z
abstract: Anastomotic stricture after biliodigestive reconstruction remains a clinical challenge leading to recurrent cholangitis, jaundice, and secondary biliary cirrhosis. Conventional plastic stents provide temporary support but are prone to biofilm formation and biliary sludge accumulation and require secondary removal procedures. There is a need for biodegradable biliary stents that provide sufficient mechanical support while actively modulating the local microenvironment. A biodegradable shape-memory biliary stent composed of a poly(CL-co-TOSUO)/BaSO4 (PCT/BaSO4) composite core coated with a decellularized human amniotic membrane-curcumin (dHAM-Cur) hydrogel was developed. In vivo performance was assessed in rat subcutaneous and duodenal implantation models and in a rabbit orthotopic common bile duct stenting model. Gut microbiota and bile metabolomic changes were analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing and untargeted Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS). The PCT/BaSO4 stent exhibited suitable mechanical properties, radiopacity, and shape memory functionality, with a degradation profile that matched the expected biliary healing period. The dHAM-Cur coating increased surface hydrophilicity and supported sustained curcumin release. The functionalized stent reduced inflammatory cell infiltration, fibrous capsule formation, and bile duct fibrosis, and preserved biliary patency compared with plastic and PCL/BaSO4 controls in vivo. Multi-omics analyses suggested that the stent subtly reshaped gut microbial composition and modulated bile acid-related metabolic pathways. The PCT/BaSO4@dHAM-Cur composite demonstrated local anti-inflammatory and anti-adhesion effects in preclinical models, along with favorable biocompatibility and anti-restenotic potential. This system holds promise as a therapeutic platform for the clinical management of biliodigestive anastomoses.

title: Inflammation-anchored injectable hydrogel integrating pathological nitric oxide scavenging and on-demand drug release for localized inflammatory bowel disease therapy.
authors: Eom S, Lee S, Boo Y, Kim J, Kim WJ
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), encompassing chronic relapsing gastrointestinal disorders, remains a profound clinical challenge because conventional therapeutics are often impeded by systemic off-target toxicities and suboptimal retention at inflamed mucosal sites. Herein, an inflammation-activated and retentive injectable hydrogel is presented, which leverages pathological nitric oxide (NO) overproduction as both a therapeutic target and an autonomous release trigger. An NO-responsive and NO-scavenging polymer (NRSP) incorporating an NO-cleavable o-phenylenediamine (o-PD) motif is formulated into cationic, dexamethasone-encapsulating micelles and electrostatically assembled with anionic hyaluronic acid (HA) to form a shear-thinning hydrogel that facilitates minimally invasive rectal administration and ensures prolonged, localized retention at the inflamed mucosal interface. Upon exposure to the NO-rich inflammatory microenvironment, structural disruption of NO-responsive and NO-scavenging micelles (NRSM) compromises the electrostatic integrity of the HA-micelle network, thereby reducing the storage modulus and accelerating cargo release. In vitro evaluations using lipopolysaccharide-stimulated macrophages demonstrate that NRSM hydrogels effectively reduce intracellular and extracellular NO levels and attenuate pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion. Furthermore, the HA matrix mediates disease-adaptive localization through CD44 receptor recognition and preferential electrostatic adhesion to positively charged inflammatory interfaces, resulting in enhanced colonic retention in DSS-induced colitis models ex vivo. Following rectal administration in DSS-induced mice, NRSM-based hydrogels significantly alleviate disease severity, reduce colonic NO and inflammatory cytokine levels, and rescue mucosal architecture and mucin-associated features. Notably, dexamethasone-loaded NRSM hydrogel exerted the most potent synergistic therapeutic benefit. Overall, this disease-responsive hydrogel platform establishes an effective localized intervention for IBD, merging intrinsic pathological NO scavenging with controlled drug delivery.

title: Hematopoietic cell transplantation using treosulfan-based conditioning for IL-10 receptor deficiency.
authors: Lakkaraja M, Schmitt EG, Sood AK, Chen K, Modi AJ, Verbsky JW, Torgerson T, Wahbeh G
abstract: IL-10 receptor deficiency is a life-threatening inborn error of immunity associated with early-onset inflammatory bowel disease. Hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) using treosulfan-based conditioning resulted in excellent survival with full donor engraftment. Importantly, anakinra effectively served as a bridge to HCT.

title: DUF6383-domain containing protein from Parabacteroides distasonis predicts survival in patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis.
authors: Kreimeyer H, Gonzalez C, Fondevila MF, AlcHepNet Investigators, Canbay A, Stärkel P, Gonzalez DJ, Schnabl B
abstract: Intestinal dysbiosis is a hallmark of alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) characterized by a higher abundance of unfavorable species and a reduction of beneficial species. In this study, we aimed to analyze the bacterial proteome of stool samples from patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) (n = 80), alcohol use disorder (AUD; n = 20), and controls (n = 19) from an international multicenter cohort using quantitative tandem mass tag (TMT)-based metaproteomic profiling. We validated our results in an independent multicenter cohort of 72 patients with AH at the genomic level using qPCR. We detected 2,364 bacterial proteins and identified distinct metaproteomic signatures separating controls, patients with AUD, and AH. Patients with AUD and AH were characterized by depletion of Firmicutes-derived proteins and enrichment of proteins from Bacteroidetes, Proteobacteria, and Actinobacteria. Eighteen bacterial proteins increased with disease severity, many with multifunctional "moonlighting" roles, including enolase and hexokinase. DUF6383 domain-containing protein from Parabacteroides distasonis is correlated with histological injury, inflammatory cell infiltration, and is linked to neutrophil degranulation in the host. Patients with a high abundance of DUF6383 domain-containing protein had significantly lower 90-day survival, and this association was validated by qPCR at the genomic level in a second cohort. Our findings show that microbial proteins are associated with disease severity and progression, and that DUF6383 domain-containing protein from P. distasonis is a potential prognostic biomarker for AH.

title: Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression and changes in the fibrosis-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment in participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD.
authors: Okuma H
abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is common in type 2 diabetes. We investigated the association between monocyte mRNA expression of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2), the molecular target of luseogliflozin, and changes in the fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index during treatment with this agent. METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study used prospectively collected peripheral blood monocyte samples from 82 participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD who had received luseogliflozin for at least 6 months. Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was measured using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Clinical and laboratory parameters, including FIB-4 index, were evaluated at baseline and 6 months after luseogliflozin initiation. Changes were calculated as the 6-month value minus the baseline value; therefore, negative values indicated reductions. RESULTS: After 6 months, waist circumference, hemoglobin A1c, liver enzyme levels, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and the FIB-4 index decreased significantly. Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was negatively correlated with the change in the FIB-4 index, indicating that higher baseline expression was associated with a greater reduction. In multiple regression analyses, natural-log-transformed baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression remained associated with the change in the FIB-4 index after adjustment for baseline clinical variables. CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was associated with a greater reduction in the FIB-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment. This finding should be interpreted as an exploratory association between a cell-specific transcriptomic feature and changes in a fibrosis-related index, rather than as evidence of functional SGLT2 signaling in monocytes or histological fibrosis regression. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13340-026-00941-2.

Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
authors: Braatz E, Stenman M, Al-Mousli J, Dalén M, Olsson C
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp (n = 261) or MHCA (n = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, p = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank p = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

title: ALMS1 stabilizes the proximal centriole to drive transition zone assembly and ciliogenesis.
authors: Phan TP, Derderian C, Herranz-Pérez V, Li KH, Burlingame AL, Reiter JF
abstract: The human ciliopathy Alström syndrome is caused by mutations in ALMS1. How ALMS1 contributes to cilia function has been unclear. Unlike other ciliopathy-associated proteins, ALMS1 localizes to the proximal end of centrioles, raising the possibility that it contributes to cilia function via a distinct mechanism. We found that, without ALMS1, centrioles are short and frequently break at their proximal ends. Truncated, broken ALMS1 mutant centrioles display reduced microtubule-organizing activity and disrupted centriole linkers. Without ALMS1, Golgi-derived cargos, including transmembrane components of the transition zone, are impaired in their trafficking to the centrosome. Consequently, ALMS1 is important for transition zone assembly, ciliogenesis, and the control of ciliary membrane composition. In mice, disruption of ALMS1 causes progressive, age-dependent loss of cilia in tissues affected in Alström syndrome, including retina, kidney, and brain. We conclude that Alström syndrome is caused by disruption of proximal centriole integrity and centrosome-directed protein trafficking, compromising ciliary assembly and maintenance.

title: Deficiency of NBAS causes immune dysregulation due to hyperactivation of IFN signaling.
authors: Liu C, Zhang L, Lu M, Shen Y, Yao Y, Liu F, Wang Q, Zhang B
abstract: NBAS deficiency is a multisystem disorder, but its immunologic manifestations and underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. Here, we expand the genotypic and phenotypic spectrum of NBAS deficiency through four patients carrying five loss-of-function NBAS mutations. Minigene assays and RNA analysis showed that these splicing or missense mutations resulted in aberrant alternative splicing. Clinically, the patients showed early-onset recurrent or persistent cytopenias and immune dysregulation, together with severe infections, inflammatory activation, and multi-organ involvement, including renal and neurologic manifestations. Transcriptomic analysis revealed overactivation of type I interferon signaling pathways compared with healthy controls, and single-cell RNA sequencing demonstrated that this upregulated inflammation was predominantly driven by myeloid cells. Together, these findings identify NBAS deficiency as a cause of immune dysregulation characterized by myeloid-driven type I interferonopathy, expand the clinical spectrum of NBAS-related disorders, and highlight the critical role of NBAS in maintaining immune homeostasis.

title: Disrupting the cholesterol-mechanics axis enables ferroptosis and deep drug delivery in hepatocellular carcinoma.
authors: Zhu J, Zhong Y, Yan S, Zeng X
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) develops within a fibrotic and stiffened microenvironment that limits drug penetration and suppresses regulated cell death, contributing to therapeutic resistance. Here we identify cholesterol as a central regulator linking extracellular matrix (ECM) mechanics to ferroptosis resistance through lipid raft‒mediated mechanotransduction. Spatial transcriptomics of human HCC specimens reveals enrichment of PTK2 (focal adhesion kinase, FAK) and cholesterol-associated pathways at tumor-stroma interfaces, implicating a cholesterol-mechanics axis in tumor progression. To target this vulnerability, we engineer a one-dimensional Fe-Mn oxyhydroxide nanozyme integrated with cholesterol oxidase (FeMnOOH/C). This platform simultaneously depletes cholesterol, disrupts lipid raft signaling, and remodels ECM stiffness, while amplifying ferroptosis through multienzymatic redox catalysis. FeMnOOH/C enhances membrane fluidity, promotes deep tumor penetration, and enables efficient intratumoral delivery of therapeutics. In vivo, FeMnOOH/C induces robust ferroptosis and immunogenic cell death, leading to increased cytotoxic T cell infiltration and marked tumor suppression. These findings establish mechano-metabolic reprogramming (mechanical regulation and cholesterol deprivation) as a strategy to overcome ferroptosis resistance and provide proof-of-concept support for a strategy of targeting fibrotic tumors.

title: Heterojunction nanozyme achieve highly efficient antibacterial by cuproptosis-like death and ferroptosis-like death.
authors: Wang W, Zhu R, Gui H, Jin X, Wei X, Wang X
abstract: Metal-ion-mediated lethal pathways offers a highly potent strategy for antibacterial treatments. However, relying on single-pathway mechanisms often fails to overwhelm bacterial antioxidant defenses, reducing antibacterial efficacy. This study designed a heterojunction nanozyme (Cu2O/Fe2O3) that induces ferroptosis-like death and copper-mediated metabolic toxicity exhibiting cuproptosis-like features, achieving highly effective antibacterial treatment. Computational chemistry analysis indicates that the Cu2O/Fe2O3 heterointerface establishes a built-in electric field through spontaneous interfacial electron transfer, thereby enhancing its peroxidase (POD)-like activity. Within the acidic bacterial microenvironment, Cu2O/Fe2O3 catalyzes the generation of large amounts of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and releases metal ions, inducing and amplifying ferroptosis-like death, which disrupts the function of ETC enzymes by attacking iron-sulfur clusters. Concurrently, copper ions disrupt the redox balance by depleting bacillithiol (BSH), indirectly increasing bacterial susceptibility and promoting ferroptosis-like death. Furthermore, the accumulation of copper ions triggers severe metabolic impairments that biochemically resemble the cuproptosis cascade, which disrupts key enzymes of the TCA cycle and impairs the synthesis of electron donors (NADH and FADH2), thereby cutting off the supply of substrates to ETC at the upstream stage. Overall, this study demonstrates that triggering bimetallic ion-mediated metabolic disruptions induces an energy crisis in bacteria, providing a reference for multimodal antibacterial strategies.

title: Label-free impedimetric immunosensor for TSH detection using Ni-Co3O4/AuNP-modified screen-printed electrodes.
authors: Panda M, Swetha R, Krishna Priya M, Divya KP, Satheesh Babu TG, Pradeep A
abstract: Rapid, accessible, and accurate detection of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) is essential for early diagnosis and effective management of thyroid disorders. This study reports the development of a label-free impedimetric immunosensor for TSH detection using flexible screen-printed carbon electrodes modified with Ni-Co3O4/AuNP. The developed sensor exhibits a wide linear detection range from 0.001 to 100 μIU/mL and a low limit of detection (LOD) of 0.001 μIU/mL, demonstrating a high sensitivity for TSH quantification. The sensor demonstrates excellent selectivity, reproducibility, and its performance is validated using serum samples, yielding recovery rates between 92.2 and 99.6%. The developed Ni-Co3O4/AuNP-based impedimetric immunosensor holds promise as a sensitive platform for point-of-care quantification of thyroid function.

title: 3D culture-derived MSC EV facilitate repair by activating microglial autophagy in spinal cord injury.
authors: Liu H, Li X, Li M, Jiu J, Zhao Y, Li D, Zhang J, Yan L
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is characterized by persistent neuroinflammation, neuronal loss, and limited tissue repair. Extracellular vesicles derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stromal cells (hUC-MSC-EVs) represent a promising cell-free therapeutic approach, although strategies for improving their bioactivity and regulating their cargo composition remain incompletely defined. Here, a gelatin microcarrier-based three-dimensional (3D) culture system was used to generate hUC-MSC-EVs. Compared with EVs generated under conventional two-dimensional (2D) culture conditions, 3D EVs reduced lesion severity, improved functional recovery, and promoted reparative-like changes in ionized calcium-binding adaptor molecule 1(Iba1)-positive microglia/macrophages in a rat SCI model. Transcriptomic, tandem-reporter, and pharmacological analyses indicated that intact autophagic processing contributes to the reparative-like phenotypic effects of 3D EVs in microglial cells. Comparative microRNA (miRNA) profiling identified miRNA-99a-5p as one of the enriched candidates, and gain- and loss-of-function experiments supported its contribution to autophagy-related and phenotype-associated responses in recipient microglia. The 3D culture condition was accompanied by increased nuclear localization of Yes-associated protein (YAP) and transcriptional coactivator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ), increased expression of Y-box binding protein 1 (YBX1), TEA domain transcription factor 4 (TEAD4) occupancy at selected YBX1 promoter regions, and higher EV-associated miR-99a-5p abundance. RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) analysis further demonstrated an association between YBX1 and miR-99a-5p. Overall, these findings indicate that 3D culture is associated with EV cargo remodeling and improved therapeutic effects after SCI, while miR-99a-5p represents one functional EV-associated cargo contributing to selected microglial responses.

title: Sulfur-doped graphitic carbon nitride/cerium tungstate nanocomposites for ultrasensitive dopamine sensing in mouse striatal tissue.
authors: Jang HG, Manikandan R, Moon SM, Mugunthan UA, Lee J, Kang GW, Park J, Yoon JH
abstract: Following the COVID-19 pandemic, the demand for rapid diagnostic tools for the highly specific and sensitive detection of disease-related biomarkers has increased significantly. Hybrid nanocomposite-modified disposable screen-printed electrodes have shown remarkable potential for the electrochemical biosensing of various biomarkers. This study reports the fabrication of a hybrid nanocomposite comprising sulfur-doped graphitic carbon nitride (S-g-C3N4) nanosheets integrated with two-dimensional cerium tungstate (CeW) for highly sensitive electrochemical dopamine detection. The synthesized S-g-C3N4@CeW hybrid nanocomposite was thoroughly characterized using field-emission scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, and electrochemical measurements. Electroanalytical performance was evaluated using differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) under optimized experimental conditions. The fabricated electrochemical sensor exhibited a wide linear concentration range for dopamine from 0.1 to 500 μM, with a low detection limit of 1.13 nM and high sensitivity of 151.69 μA μM-1 cm-2. Finally, the fabricated sensor was used for the ex-vivo determination of dopamine in Parkinson's disease-induced mouse striatum-tissue samples, achieving good accuracy with recovery rates of 92.0 to 101.4%. This study demonstrates a promising strategy for fabricating hybrid nanocomposite-modified disposable electrochemical sensors for neurotransmitter detection in animal-disease models.

title: A tunable brain-targeted PEGylated ginsenoside Rg1 derivative disrupts the ROS-mediated inflammasome-pyroptosis cascade to ameliorate Alzheimer's cognitive deficits.
authors: Zhu X, Liang H, Fan L, Bo J, Diao F, Qian Y, Zhang G, Li W
abstract: The pathogenic cascade of oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and pyroptosis serves as a core driving factor in the pathogenesis and progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Although ginsenoside Rg1 exhibits pleiotropic neuroprotective activities, its poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability severely hinders its clinical translation. To overcome this limitation, a brain-targeted delivery system was constructed using a covalent conjugation strategy, linking purified Rg1 with rhodamine B-modified polyethylene glycol (PEG) of varying chain lengths (Rg1s-PEG). After screening, the derivative Rg1s-PEG-600 was identified as achieving an optimal balance between hydrophilic stealth properties and steric hindrance, demonstrating enhanced brain accumulation and favorable biosafety profiles. In both in vitro and in vivo models of lipopolysaccharide-induced acute neuroinflammation, Rg1s-PEG-600 attenuated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, inhibited canonical neuronal pyroptosis mediated by the NLRP1/3 inflammasomes, and significantly ameliorated behavioral deficits and synaptic loss. Furthermore, in chronic 5xFAD transgenic mice, systemic administration of Rg1s-PEG-600 for 12 weeks markedly reversed spatial memory decline, anxiety-like behavior, and synaptic protein depletion. Mechanistic studies further revealed that this targeted nanotherapeutic not only suppressed the ROS-NLRP1 signaling axis and subsequent neuronal pyroptosis in the AD brain but also comprehensively inhibited amyloidogenesis and Tau hyperphosphorylation. This work provides a promising, multitarget nanotherapeutic strategy to overcome BBB limitations and disrupt the complex pathological networks underlying neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Ultrasound-triggered spinal cord-mimetic electroactive hydrogel enables localized bioelectrical modulation and promotes spinal cord injury repair through JNK-mediated autophagy.
authors: Su X, Tian J, Zhang Z, Zhang L, Zhao Y, Zhao Y, Zhao S, Zhang Y
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) creates a hostile microenvironment that severely limits neural regeneration and functional recovery. Although bioelectrical modulation has emerged as a promising strategy for SCI repair, existing biomaterials generally provide either passive electrical conduction or stimulus-responsive electrical generation, but rarely integrate both properties within a mechanically compliant scaffold suitable for spinal cord repair. Here, we developed an injectable, remotely activatable electroactive hydrogel (SMT) by integrating conductive MXene nanosheets into a silk fibroin/tannic acid matrix, endowing the scaffold with tissue-matched mechanics, continuous electrical conductivity, and stimulus-responsive electrical output. Upon ultrasound activation, SMT generated localized bioelectrical cues within the lesion site. At the cellular level, SMT exhibited intrinsic antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects that were further enhanced by ultrasound activation, while SMT + US promoted autophagic flux through Ca2+-dependent JNK signaling. In a rat model of SCI, the ultrasound-activated hydrogel promoted neural tissue repair and remyelination, attenuated reactive gliosis, and improved functional recovery. Collectively, this study presents a remotely activatable electroactive hydrogel for SCI repair and provides a promising strategy for dynamic bioelectrical regulation during SCI repair.

title: Regulating the iron-ROS cycle via electronic structure-engineered nanoregulators for Parkinson's disease therapy.
authors: Qin Y, Xu J, Boyer C, Prince S, Kang H, Akhtar M, Wang Y, Huang R
abstract: Iron-driven reactive oxygen species (ROS) amplification forms a self-sustaining pathological cycle in Parkinson's disease (PD), yet remains difficult to therapeutically interrupt due to the lack of strategies that coordinate metal homeostasis and redox regulation. Here, we report an electronic-structure-engineered nanoregulatory strategy that regulates the iron-ROS cycle rather than passively scavenging ROS. Nitrogen-doped, herbal-derived carbon dots (CD) were rationally constructed to establish a conjugated electronic framework, in which heteroatom-induced electron delocalization defined redox-active sites and governed the coupling between iron chelation and catalytic ROS regulation. This structure-electronic state-function relationship enabled programmable disruption of the iron-ROS feedback loop at its source. Functionally, the nanoregulators achieved low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 (LRP1)-mediated brain delivery, exhibited efficient central nervous system exposure, and underwent brain clearance via the cerebrospinal fluid pathway. At the cellular level, they restored mitochondrial function, suppressed ferroptosis-associated lipid peroxidation, and reprogramed stress-related pathways toward neuronal survival. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed coordinated regulation of redox, metabolic, and inflammatory networks. In Parkinsonian mice, this strategy reduced iron deposition, preserved dopaminergic neurons, and improved motor function. Integration with levodopa further enabled sustained, disease-modifying neuroprotection.
